objective: At the owner's request ('Yes, please continue', approving COUNT-TFNP-20261107-001's recommendation (i)): decide whether the surface on which a knot space's incidence graph is embedded (its Euler characteristic and orientability) decides whether the knot's count forces a contradiction and which TFNP class it then has. Prove the parity and Euler-count identities for signed cubic triple systems on any closed surface (all-odd signs exist iff the Euler characteristic is even; with them, violated lines minus the faces' excess agreements equals half the Euler characteristic), and settle satisfiability of the triangular-lattice knot spaces on the torus, the Klein bottle and the projective plane for every class of signs. Serves the complexity program (the complexity of the knot's spaces) and the space intuition (whether logic's count reads the surface); standalone value relative to the nearest known work: the agreement-count analogue of Kasteleyn's parity condition on surfaces (Kasteleyn 1963; Tesler 2000 for non-orientable surfaces), set against Friedl-Ivanyos-Santha-Verhoeven's result that Sperner's class drops to PPA on non-orientable surfaces.
status: Complete 2026-11-07: on every closed surface violated lines minus the faces' excess agreements equal (chi - |D|)/2, so the knot's count forces a violated line only on the sphere with Kasteleyn signs and an over-agreeing face when chi < |D|; it never uses orientation and wherever it forces lies in PPADS^dt (never PPA-hard, unlike Sperner). Satisfying assignments are perfect matchings in the homology class the signs prescribe. Lattice tori: a class is satisfiable iff the slope triangle has an integer point of matching parity, so only degenerate, even thin and the two Fano tori fail; simple Klein bottles, projective planes and genus-2 covers are satisfiable in every tested class. Recommendation: Research directions, (i) negative curvature's count (2/3); (ii) return to question 9 with laws that build their own surface (2/3; owner's call).
stop_rule: Stop when the identities are proved and satisfiability is settled for the torus, Klein bottle and projective-plane lattice families in every sign class (with any small exceptions explained), and the resulting class of each forcing family is proved or the gap named.
title: The knot's count on surfaces: does the Euler characteristic decide it?
